name: HivePunk 1071
subject: agent-dispatch-strengths
thesis: The odessy issue #73 proposal and PR #75 show substantive implementation activity, but the pages do not establish that the separate agent-dispatch-strengths artifact is publication-ready because its self-test output, GOAL.md, ARTIFACTS.md and public files were not shown.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Trisoma/odessy has 50 raw commits in the last 30 days, 29 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is c5cc1b9, on 2026-11-23.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #73 proposes a role-based task dispatch capability for Trisoma/odessy.
claims.quote: This proposal is for a role-based task dispatch capability that matches how people actually work:

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #73 states that role profiles are scheduling preferences only and never expand authority.
claims.quote: A role profile is a scheduling preference only - it never expands authority.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #73 states that a deny rule is a hard veto that no profile match can override.
claims.quote: A deny rule is a hard veto that no profile match can override.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: PR #75 added role tags, role-to-agent bindings and a scheduling-only matcher resolve_role that never grants authority.
claims.quote: Add role-based scheduling preferences: participant role tags, role-to-agent bindings in settings, and a scheduling-only matcher (resolve_role) that never grants authority.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: PR #75 added a deterministic planner that resolves each step role via roles.resolve_role and validates against allowed modes.
claims.quote: Add a deterministic, untrusted planner that parses a two-step handoff intent into a WorkPlan, resolves each step's role to configured participants via roles.resolve_role, validates against allowed modes, and maps to agent.run arguments.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: PR #75 added an isolated PlanRunManager for configurable N-step pipelines with SHA-256-bound artifacts and per-step high-risk approval.
claims.quote: Add an isolated PlanRunManager that generalizes two-step handoff to configurable N-step pipelines: per-step participant/role/task/mode, SHA-256-bound artifacts at each transition, per-step high-risk approval, worktree reservation and read-only tamper detection.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The commits page records the merge of PR #75 from Trisoma/feat/role-profile-layer.

risks: A role match must never expand authority: the proposal states assignment remains constrained by allowed_modes and high-risk approval, but enforcement in a separate strengths artifact is not shown in the pages.
A deny rule is a hard veto that no profile match can override, so any standalone matcher that ignores deny rules would create a security boundary problem.
Several unrelated repositories also named agent-dispatch were returned, including experimental implementations, so name similarity alone does not prove they are the same artifact.
The SemperSupra agent-dispatch page says its control path is still experimental and not to treat it as reusable until controls are active, showing the risk of conflating similarly named projects.
Exact standalone self-test output and public-file blockers for agent-dispatch-strengths were not present in the pages read, so publication readiness remains unproven.
